P1.evidence: No setter suffix in the title and no application or setter notes referenced, so P1a does not apply. The frame was delivered but compressed to three parts: 'go into what you'd actually like to achieve with your fitness, see where you're currently at. And also, if we can help you bridge that gap. And if I feel like we can, take you through how' — 'what's in the way' is only implied and 'what you need' is absent. No frame agreement was sought; the rep went straight on. The open question ran verbatim: 'what is it that you're potentially looking to get some help with from us?'

P2.evidence: Age (32) and weight (68 kg) asked directly; the height question is garbled in transcript but was asked and answered. Occupation was volunteered by the prospect ('my job is heavy in terms of hours'), not asked, though the rep did then probe the physical demands: 'do you have specific movements when you're working, for example, that you feel like I just lose or lack some mobility here?'. Injuries and restrictions were screened properly and with emphasis: 'any like restrictions or any injuries or something, nothing like that, because it's very important to know'. Hereditary and general health conditions were never asked. Training frequency and results emerged from the prospect's own account rather than direct questions. Diet was properly probed ('is that like sort of the usual day-to-day structure?'). Sleep was never raised at all, and daily energy was never asked — the prospect volunteered 'feeling less tired' as a goal.

P3.evidence: Strong on the surface layer, weak on the deep layer. Mobility, strength and cardio were directly asked ('is mobility something that you feel like you need to work on?'). But the four scripted depth questions were all skipped: no 'something physical you want to do but can't', no 'outside of the physical, what's actually driving this right now?', no 'when you're moving better, what does that actually do for you?', no 'who else does that impact?'. The deep material — leadership, confidence, competing in Hong Kong, starting a family — was volunteered unprompted by the prospect, and the rep echoed rather than excavated it: 'you also just want to become better overall when you're also mentioning, of course, build a family in the future.' The rep did run a long, accurate recap with a confirmation check ('So that's like the big picture, or is there something that's missing there?'), but it stayed on physical outcomes and never made the 'this isn't really about the weight, it's about X' reframe.

P4.evidence: Essentially unrun as a phase. The rep confirmed history only in passing ('you have been doing kettlebells for six years, right?'). The prospect supplied the entire root-cause picture himself — the Maverick app shutting down, training alone with bad technique, work crowding it out, and the gap he wanted filled: 'I'm actually looking for something where someone can really follow up, right?'. Because he volunteered it and the rep never asked, the credit is partial at best. None of the diagnostic questions ran: no 'what happened with that?', no 'why do you feel it didn't stick?', no 'what's the one thing actually getting in the way?', and no 'the information isn't the problem — why can't you stick to it on your own?'.

P5.evidence: The Consequence Frame was skipped in its entirety. There is no two-year projection, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for?', no 'why not?', and no line-in-the-sand question anywhere in the call. The rep moved from the goals recap straight into presenting the three pillars. This is the single largest structural gap in the call and it is the phase that would have built the urgency needed to survive the payment objection later.

P6.evidence: The belief question ran well: 'when it comes to the training, nutrition, accountability, do you feel like if those are all put together for you... you're actually going to be able to stick to that, and also then to actually get to the goals?' — answered 'Yeah, that's the whole idea' and then 'I'm definitely ready to commit to it.' The all-in isolation question was only gestured at ('if you feel like, I don't know, Richard, then there's no use case in talking further about it') rather than asked, so no blockers were surfaced before price. Critically, the phase ran out of order: the script requires a genuine verbal yes BEFORE presenting anything, but the rep presented all three pillars from 00:21 to 00:34 and only then ran the commitment check.

P11.evidence: Payment was only partially collected — $200 against a $6,000 offer, and framed as reversible rather than as a purchase. An onboarding slot with Trevor was verbally agreed for Wednesday 8 July at 07:15, but the invite actually sent and accepted was for a 10 July call with the rep himself, so the Trevor booking cannot be confirmed. The agreement email was never mentioned, and nothing was signed on the call. Community access was named but deferred as contingent on payment ('I can also book that meeting with him and get you access to the community'); a pre-meeting document was sent, but there was no welcome email and no Skool link.

objection_plays.detail: Triggered squarely by 'Are you guys requiring a full payment ahead? Or, like, you're splitting it or so?' and 'I was expecting, like, kind of a monthly rating'. The rep never isolated — 'Finances aside, nothing else keeping you from 100%?' was not asked — so it was never established that money was the only blocker. He did run the cash-on-hand element, and persistently: 'What will be possible for you today, just so I have an idea?' and 'So is it like just nothing available at the moment?'. Everything else in the financial picture was skipped: no monthly surplus after bills, no credit card count, no available credit, no used-versus-available, no crypto or investments. The 'you're not in a SHOULD I place, you're in a HOW place' reframe was not used, and the 'most clients pay upfront, but for some we break it up' line was approximated ('Usually, people put it all up front for their own accountability sometimes') but not converted into a structured plan.

Script gap. The prospect's objection was not incapacity to pay but a mismatched billing expectation — he had budgeted for a monthly subscription and had not conceived of a lump sum: 'I didn't plan any amount or anything about this.' The playbook has no play for an instalment-expectation objection, so the rep improvised a $100-$200 reversible holding deposit to keep the deal alive. That is a gap in the script rather than a rep failure, and it is the second time this corpus has produced an objection that Objection C's capacity-to-pay framing does not fit.

notes: Warm, patient discovery on the surface layer and a genuinely well-delivered three-pillar presentation, but the back half of the diagnostic never ran: Past Attempts was almost entirely prospect-led and the Consequence Frame was skipped outright. With no cost-of-inaction established and the commitment check run after the presentation rather than before it, the rep reached price with nothing to hold against a cashflow objection and had to invent a deposit. Coach on running P5 and on isolating before opening the wallet.
